newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolian riders mark festival shorn of politics.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian riders mark festival shorn of politics.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Mongolians have travelled on horseback and on foot to the nation's capital for the Nadaam festival, an annual pageant of horsemanship, wrestling and archery.

Mongolians from across the vast, landlocked country on Sunday marked the culmination of the summer festival -- the first in 76 years that did not commemorate the nation's communist revolution of 1921.
The reformist parliament that ousted the ex-communist government in elections last year renamed the pageant the National Nadaam Festival, stripping it of its political overtones.

Herdsmen in their high boots and colourful traditional dress camped out on the grasslands on the outskirts of the capital for three days of contests in what are known as the "three manly sports" of horsemanship, archery and wrestling.

Nearly 3,000 horses with riders as young as six years old dashed across the plains while more than 100 men and women shot bone-headed arrows at leather targets up to 100 metres (yards) away to earn the title of top marksman.
Some 500 wrestlers grappled for the titles of "Lion" and "Falcon" with the victors performing a ritual "Eagle" dance around the capital's stadium.
Celebrations began on Friday morning when soldiers carried banners from parliament to the stadium where President Natsagiin Bagabandi officially opened the festival.
